node.statement: F2 LITERATURE ANCHOR — the summit confirmed open at a named 2024-25 frontier (2026-07-10, campaign cycle 94). SEARCH VERDICT on 'square-root cancellation for generalized Gauss-lemma parities of subgroup orbit configurations': (1) CLOSEST LIVING WORK: Borda-Munsch-Shparlinski, 'Pointwise and correlation bounds on Dedekind sums over small subgroups' (Research in Number Theory 2024; arXiv 2305.04304) — Dedekind sums s(lambda, p) for lambda of small multiplicative order, whose method 'relates high moments of L(1,chi) over subgroups of characters to correlations of Dedekind sums' — the SAME bridge our satellites 16-18 built independently (mutual validation of the campaign's frame by concurrent literature). Their theory bounds the SIZES of subgroup Dedekind sums, with results optimal only assuming the infinitude of Mersenne primes — the size theory alone is at the edge of current technology. The PARITY/carry-count cancellation theory (our summit) does not appear. (2) The generalized-polynomial pseudorandomness school (newest: Madritsch-Tichy 2025, arXiv 2509.19810 — well-distribution measures for floor-polynomial binary sequences) covers exactly eps's FUNCTION CLASS but over intervals/APs and with measures far weaker than the needed exp(S)-weighted 2^{o(n)} cancellation; subgroup-orbit domains absent. (3) Gauss-lemma generalizations in the literature require HALF-SYSTEMS (A disjoint-union -A = all classes); our G has -G = G — maximally non-half-system, which is exactly why no classical symbol identity exists (consistent with satellites 26-27). CONCLUSION (the campaign's D3 deliverable, self-executed): the summit is a genuinely open problem one step beyond a named, active research frontier: Borda-Munsch-Shparlinski bound subgroup Dedekind sum SIZES; the prize needs PARITY cancellation of subgroup carry counts under Gaussian weights. Brief v4 updated with both anchors. Sources: arxiv.org/abs/2305.04304, arxiv.org/abs/2509.19810, arxiv.org/pdf/math/0311453 (Duke-Hopkins), en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zolotarev%27s_lemma. Twenty-eighth satellite; the identification AND literature programs are both complete. BMS DEEP-READ ADDENDUM (cycle 96, full text of arXiv 2305.04304): (i) CONFIRMED from the body — their machinery is continued-fraction size bounds (Barkan-Hickerson: |s(a,b)| <= (1/12) sum of partial quotients) plus a cyclotomic-norm Liouville lemma (h lambda = m mod p forces |m|+|h| >= p^{1/phi(d)}); explicitly NO results on signs, parities, or distribution mod small integers — the summit's content is absent from the frontier's strongest paper. (ii) THE MERSENNE WARNING, DISARMED: their extremal family s(2, 2^d-1) ~ p/24 (maximal size, zero cancellation, order-d element) requires q-1 of 2-adic valuation 1; official-shape rows force n | q-1 with n a 2-power >= 16 (KoalaBear p-1 = 2^24 * 127), so the ONLY known degeneracy family for subgroup sawtooth objects is STRUCTURALLY EXCLUDED from every row the prize touches — a small unconditional safety theorem for the summit. (iii) TRANSFERABLE LEADS QUEUED: the Barkan-Hickerson sign term (-1)^{n-1}/8 makes CF-DEPTH PARITY the literature's only explicit parity mechanism for sawtooth objects (a possible route to K mod 2: express the orbit's floor-sum parity through CF depths of orbit points a x^2/q); the cyclotomic-norm lemma transfers as a bound on partial quotients of orbit points. Both are research programs, recorded for the opportunistic-lead rotation and the delegation channel. SOURCE AUDIT COMPLETE (cycle 100): every reference in brief v4 now read at depth with verdicts. (iv) DUKE-HOPKINS (read in full): their quadratic symbol (a/G) = sign of the a-power permutation on conjugacy classes satisfies (a/G) = (d/a) via Galois action on the character-table determinant (sigma_a(sqrt d) = (a/G) sqrt d) — the mechanism STRUCTURALLY produces Dirichlet characters in a and nothing else; since eps(a) is measured to be no character (satellite 26), the ENTIRE class of permutation-sign/Galois-twist mechanisms is excluded — a strengthening of cycle 93's naive-Zolotarev refutation to the full DH framework. (v) ZAGIER higher-dimensional Dedekind sums: (n+1)-term reciprocity for COTANGENT PRODUCTS at LINEAR arguments with pairwise-coprime moduli — shape mismatch with our single-sawtooth polynomial-argument subgroup sums; no direct application (brief v4 E2 qualified accordingly). (vi) NOTED for future reading: 'Higher dimensional Dedekind sums in finite fields' (J. Number Theory 2011-ish, ScienceDirect S1071579711000438) — the finite-field Dedekind literature is the one unread adjacent shelf. The delegation brief's references are now all personally vetted; no promise in it rests on an unread source. SHELF CLOSED — LITERATURE PROGRAM TERMINAL (cycle 101): the finite-field higher Dedekind sums literature (Hamahata; Bayad-Hamahata: JNT 2011/2014, Acta Arith. 2012) is DRINFELD-MODULE theory — sums valued in function-field completions with char-p reciprocity identities; no archimedean sawtooth, no parity content, no transfer to real-valued carry counts. The newest cone machinery (Torres-Nova, arXiv 2512.20542, Dec 2025: Dedekind-Rademacher reciprocity for absolutely continuous test functions via conical zeta values) generalizes the TEST FUNCTION but not the INDEX SET — full-range sums only, no subgroup restriction, no mod-2 refinement. FINAL LITERATURE VERDICT: across the classical shelf (Gauss/Eisenstein/Zolotarev/Rademacher), the modern frontier (Borda-Munsch-Shparlinski sizes), the group-theoretic generalizations (Duke-Hopkins — characters only), the higher-dimensional theory (Zagier — shape mismatch), the function-field theory (Hamahata-Bayad — wrong valuation), and the newest cone methods (index-set limitation), NO parity theory for restricted-index sawtooth sums exists anywhere adjacent. The summit's one-sentence problem is beyond the entire visible literature; the campaign's map of the boundary is complete. Sources added: semanticscholar Finite Dedekind Sums (Hamahata), sciencedirect S1071579714000215, arXiv 2512.20542.
